title: External testing measured mortality-model performance in sepsis-associated liver injury
summary: Models using first-24-hour features predicted 7-, 14- and 28-day in-hospital mortality. In an external cohort of 229 patients, AUROCs were 0.720, 0.717 and 0.763; the 28-day model exceeded modified SOFA and MELD-Na in this cohort, but transportability was moderate and 14-day calibration imperfect. A correction clarified that the analysis used first-24-hour data. Retrospective prognostic performance does not establish treatment benefit; the authors call for prospective multicenter validation.
ai_technology: Interpretable supervised machine-learning models with SHAP analysis
